failure_reason: The long_tx injector did not hold sufficiently contentious locks on hot TPC-C keys long enough or broadly enough across warehouses, so Innodb_row_lock_time did not rise, blocked_session_count stayed low, no slow queries were recorded (likely due to slow_query_log/threshold), and the resultant blocking did not affect enough of the workload to cause a >=30% QPS drop. Lock_contention showed more waits, but waits were short and not widespread. The chain thus broke at long_tx→lock_contention causality and never materialized slow_query or qps_drop.
suggested_changes: Broaden and intensify the lock scope to hot TPC-C rows across multiple warehouses so a meaningful fraction of terminals are blocked: hold row locks on district (d_w_id,d_id) and stock (s_w_id,s_i_id) for w_id IN (1,2,3,4) and s_i_id BETWEEN 1 AND 200 inside a single transaction, then sleep without committing.

Increase long_tx hold time: set duration_sec to at least 180–300 seconds and keep the transaction open (no commit) during this window (e.g., SELECT SLEEP(120) inside the transaction) to push Innodb_row_lock_time and row_lock_time_avg up.

Raise blocker concurrency moderately (e.g., 4) to cover multiple warehouses without causing avoidable deadlocks. If you use higher concurrency, shard each session to disjoint warehouse sets to avoid overlapping lock sets.
Force pessimistic locking and next-key behavior: SET SESSION TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL REPEATABLE READ and use explicit SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on indexed predicates; do not use NOWAIT/SKIP LOCKED.

Ensure workload alignment: target at least 4 out of 10 warehouses (40% of terminals) to make a >=30% QPS drop achievable under the TPC-C mix (New-Order ~45% and Payment ~43% will both wait on district locks).

Keep waiters from timing out prematurely: SET SESSION innodb_lock_wait_timeout=120 for the background workload sessions if possible; at minimum, set it in the blocker sessions to avoid rolling back early.

Enable slow query detection during the run: SET GLOBAL slow_query_log=ON and reduce long_query_time to 0.2s (or lower) before the lock hold, so blocked transactions are counted as slow queries; restore afterward.

If the above still yields insufficient QPS drop, switch to gap-lock-heavy blocking on New-Order inserts: within the same long_tx transaction, run SELECT no_o_id FROM new_order FORCE INDEX(PRIMARY) WHERE no_w_id IN (1,2,3,4) AND no_d_id BETWEEN 1 AND 10 AND no_o_id > 0 FOR UPDATE; then sleep. This creates next-key locks that will block inserts in those districts.

If your current injected_nodes set only includes long_tx and your harness cannot set global slow log variables or shard blocking by warehouse, you may need to add supporting injected_nodes or driver-side controls in a future iteration; otherwise the slow_query and qps_drop nodes may remain under-triggered.

long_tx.sql_text: BEGIN; SET SESSION TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL REPEATABLE READ; SET SESSION innodb_lock_wait_timeout=120; /* District locks block New-Order and Payment */ SELECT d_id FROM district FORCE INDEX(PRIMARY) WHERE d_w_id IN (1,2,3,4) FOR UPDATE; /* Stock locks block New-Order item updates */ SELECT s_i_id FROM stock FORCE INDEX(PRIMARY) WHERE s_w_id IN (1,2,3,4) AND s_i_id BETWEEN 1 AND 200 FOR UPDATE; /* Hold locks long enough to trigger slow queries and QPS drop */ SELECT SLEEP(120); ROLLBACK;
long_tx.pre_sql: SET GLOBAL slow_query_log=ON; SET GLOBAL long_query_time=0.2;
long_tx.notes: If needed, alternative to intensify blocking: add before SLEEP() -> SELECT no_o_id FROM new_order FORCE INDEX(PRIMARY) WHERE no_w_id IN (1,2,3,4) AND no_d_id BETWEEN 1 AND 10 AND no_o_id > 0 FOR UPDATE;

risk_warning: These changes deliberately hold many row and gap locks across multiple hot warehouses and will significantly impact availability: expect high lock waits, potential deadlocks, and a substantial QPS drop. Enabling slow query log and lowering long_query_time are global and may increase log volume; restore to your baseline after the test. Run only in non-production, monitor deadlocks/aborts, and ensure you have privilege to change GLOBAL variables. To minimize deadlocks, avoid overlapping lock ranges across concurrent blocker sessions.
